title: Champagne truffles
subtitle: dark chocolate ganache truffles flavoured with champagne and finished in cocoa powder
excerpt: Champagne truffles are dark chocolate ganache made with a reduction of champagne or sparkling wine stirred into the cream. The ganache is chilled until firm, shaped into small rounds, and rolled in sifted cocoa powder. The champagne gives the ganache a faint sharpness that cuts through the richness of the chocolate.
sourceNotes: Chocolate truffles originated in France in the late nineteenth century. The champagne-and-dark-chocolate combination appears in French and British confectionery books from the mid-twentieth century onward, most commonly as a celebration confection.

recipe.freezeNotes: Freeze uncoated in a single layer for up to 2 months. Roll in cocoa powder after thawing.
recipe.makeAheadNotes: Keeps refrigerated for up to 2 weeks. Roll in cocoa just before serving.

content.text: Champagne truffles are a dark chocolate ganache made with champagne or sparkling wine reduced into the cream, giving the ganache a faint acidity that lifts the chocolate. The reduction concentrates the flavour; a large glass of champagne cooks down to two or three tablespoons of liquid in about 10 minutes. The ganache is chilled until firm, shaped into rounds, and rolled in cocoa powder.
Pour the champagne into a small saucepan and bring to a simmer. Cook over medium heat for 10 to 12 minutes until reduced to about 3 tablespoons. Add the cream and heat until just below the boil.
Put the chopped chocolate in a heatproof bowl. Pour the hot cream-champagne mixture over the chocolate and leave for 1 minute without stirring.
Stir slowly from the centre outward until the ganache is smooth and glossy. Add the butter and stir until fully incorporated.
Pour into a shallow dish. Press cling film directly onto the surface. Refrigerate for at least 2 hours until firm enough to scoop.
Spread the sifted cocoa powder in a shallow dish. Scoop the ganache and roll into balls between cool palms. Drop each ball into the cocoa and roll to coat. Place on a tray lined with baking paper.
Refrigerate for 30 minutes to firm. Serve at room temperature.

attrs.problem: Ganache too liquid to hold its shape when scooped
attrs.avoid: Avoid skipping the champagne reduction; excess liquid will keep the ganache soft.
attrs.fix: Reduce the champagne thoroughly before adding the cream. Chill the ganache for an extra hour. If still too soft, stir in 30 g of extra chocolate melted separately.

attrs.problem: Cocoa coating falling off or looking patchy
attrs.avoid: Avoid rolling truffles that are too warm; the cocoa does not stick evenly to a soft surface.
attrs.fix: Work quickly with cold hands and chill the scooped ganache for 5 minutes before rolling. If the coating is still thin, roll each truffle again in fresh cocoa after the first coat has dried slightly.
